latency_and_throughput_audit.why_cross_row_is_two: row_ready requires both row_active_q and pipe_valid_q to be false and has no same-cycle look-ahead from the last accepted update; the next row is accepted one cycle after the prior row update and produces its update one cycle later
latency_and_throughput_audit.safe_ii_claim: II=1 is demonstrated for consecutive predecoded groups within one active multi-group row, not for arbitrary row transactions

pipeline_storage_audit.safe_storage_claim: 1,920 bits is the registered pair-sum payload only; it is not the total M127 pipeline or control-state storage

P1.title: The unqualified no-backpressure II=1 field overstates row-level throughput
P1.evidence: Four groups predecoded from one 16-source row accept on four consecutive cycles, but four consecutive legal single-group K4 rows produce accepted updates exactly two cycles apart. RTL row_ready requires !row_active_q && !pipe_valid_q, so it cannot accept the next row on the prior row's last-update cycle.
P1.required_fix: Rename the admitted metric to intra_row_group_update_ii=1 and publish cross_row_single_group_update_ii=2, or add last-group look-ahead that can accept and launch the next row without a bubble and reverify identity under backpressure.

P2.title: 1,920 bits is pair-sum payload, not total pipeline storage
P2.finding: The two 96x10 pair-sum arrays are exactly 1,920 bits. Valid, block, row, selected mask and last add another 30 bits, for at least 1,950 elastic-stage bits; predecoded group and row state is additional.
P2.required_fix: Keep pair_sum_pipeline_payload_bits=1920 and report total sequential storage separately after synthesis.

P2.title: First-group zero-cycle wording is differential rather than absolute
P2.finding: A no-stall row accept produces its first accepted update one cycle later in both M125 and M127. The verified quantity is zero additional cycles versus M125, not zero absolute latency.
P2.required_fix: Always retain the _vs_m125 qualifier and report absolute first-group latency as one cycle.

P2.title: No matched DC frequency or physical speedup evidence exists yet
P2.finding: VCS proves function and cycle behavior but cannot establish timing closure, area, power or a physical speedup from the inserted registers.
P2.required_fix: Keep frequency and physical speedup false until matched exact-SHA Synopsys DC/STA comparison is independently admitted.

P2.title: The 1,536-byte weight cache remains behavioral multi-read storage
P2.finding: M127 still selects four full 768-bit source vectors from logic-array storage per launched update; no foundry SRAM/macro porting, banking cost or energy is included.
P2.required_fix: Do not convert the logical cache capacity or read width into macro PPA or energy claims before a realizable memory implementation.

paper_safe_statement: Exact-SHA commercial VCS plus an independent M125 differential scoreboard verify M127 legal accepted-cycle behavior, canonical K1-K4 grouping, exact signed arithmetic including -512/+512, 63-cycle elastic stalls, block/cache identity and reset isolation. M127 sustains II=1 for four consecutive groups within one active 16-source row; consecutive single-group K4 rows remain II=2. The 1,920-bit figure is pair-sum payload and first-group latency is one cycle with zero additional cycles versus M125. Frequency, physical speedup, macro PPA, system speedup and headline claims remain unadmitted.
prohibited_claims: Do not describe M127 as arbitrary-row or transaction-level II=1.
Do not call first_group_extra_cycles=0 zero absolute latency.
Do not call 1,920 bits the entire elastic pipeline or total sequential overhead.
Do not claim frequency, physical speedup, PPA, energy, FPS or system speedup from VCS.
